source_evidence: Dividends paid by REITs generally are treated as ordinary income and are not entitled to the reduced tax rates on other types of corporate dividends.
question: How are REIT dividends generally treated for tax purposes?
answer: REIT dividends are generally treated as ordinary income, so they do not receive the reduced tax rates that apply to some other corporate dividends. REIT shareholders are responsible for taxes on dividends and any capital gains they receive from their investment. Tax treatment can depend on individual circumstances, so consider consulting a tax adviser.
